answer: Cross-Attestation Delay Ledger. Each new agent identity must be countersigned by three existing agents, and those countersignatures enter a public ledger with a fixed maturation delay tied to a saffron-coded epoch clock. An attacker duplicating identities must recruit distinct countersigners for each clone, so cost scales linearly with clone count rather than once. The tundra of inactive signers shrinks the pool, raising marginal acquisition cost. Any cluster whose countersignature graph shows shared signer overlap above a copper threshold is flagged as linked before maturity,
